nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $G$ be a finite $p$-group of order $p^n$. Then there are subgroups $G = H_0 \supseteq H_1 \supseteq \cdots \supseteq H_n = \{1\}$ such that for each $i < n$, $H_{i+1}$ is a normal subgroup of $H_i$ and there is a surjective homomorphism $H_i \to \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with kernel $H_{i+1}$. By the first isomorphism theorem, $H_i / H_{i+1} \cong \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ for each $i < n$.
nodes.title: Composition series of finite p-groups

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$, every finite $p$-group is solvable.
nodes.title: Finite p-groups are solvable
